subject: Hosted API capacity & rate-plan followup and next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API capacity & rate-plan followup and next steps

Thanks again for the demo earlier, Alex — great to meet you and Sarah. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on so we can scope the Hosted evaluation.

What we heard:
- Priority: fast time-to-value; HealthSync prefers Hosted API to move quickly.
- Needs: low-latency reads for conversation assistants and batch summarization jobs for medical notes.
- Questions: endpoint names, supported streaming, default rate limits and options to increase burst, and data residency / PHI handling.

Ask from us (so we can size the eval and get the quickstart environment):
1) Traffic sample: typical RPS and requests per minute at peak, plus a CSV sample (see attached template).
2) Average and 95th percentile token lengths for user inputs and completions (approx).
3) Any strict VPC/KMS or on-prem requirement for PHI.

What Redwood will provide for the Hosted eval:
- Quickstart project with two endpoints (/v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings) and a short test harness.
- Baseline rate limits and a proposed burst allowance for the trial.
- A short SLA note and retention defaults; we can propose stricter retention/keys for PHI workloads if needed.

Attachments: redwood_quickstart_guide.pdf, traffic_sample_template.csv

Proposed next steps:
- Alex to share the filled traffic sample and basic token stats by tomorrow EOD.
- Marcus will confirm the rate-plan matrix and recommended caps based on the sample.
- Schedule 30-min tech kickoff next week to provision the Hosted eval keys and walk through streaming.

If Hosted won't meet the data controls, we can outline Dedicated/Private options — we'll include decision criteria in that session.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@healthsync.com>

Date: 2026-11-15T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity & rate-plan followup and next steps

Thanks Rachel — appreciated the clear recap. Quick answers from our side below so you can start sketching the plan.

Traffic & tokens:
- Peak: ~20 RPS sustained during business hours (US PST), with minute-level spikes to ~350 requests/minute during batch jobs.
- Typical concurrent user flows are short (a single 1-3 turn chat); average tokens per request (input+expected completion) ~120; 95th ~400.

Requirements:
- Latency: p95 below 400ms for the chat endpoint is preferred, but we can tolerate up to 800ms during large batch jobs.
- Data controls: We process PHI. We prefer Hosted if data segregation and encryption-at-rest+TLS in transit suffice; otherwise Dedicated or Private may be required.
- Streaming: yes — we use streaming for chat to reduce perceived latency.

I'll attach a filled traffic_sample.csv and our internal SLA questionnaire (healthsync_sla_request.pdf). Also: can you confirm the exact endpoint names and whether token-based metering or request-based metering is used for the trial?

Best,
Alex
Alex Tan
Head of Platform Engineering, HealthSync
alex.tan@healthsync.com

---
Attachment: traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 12KB)
Attachment: healthsync_sla_request.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity & rate-plan followup and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks for the details, that traffic profile maps cleanly to our Hosted offering for an eval. A few technical clarifications and what I'd recommend for the trial: 

Endpoints we will provision for the quickstart (Hosted API):
- POST /v1/chat/completions (streaming supported, SSE + chunked streaming)
- POST /v1/completions (sync)
- POST /v1/embeddings (batch-friendly)
- Health and metrics endpoints for latency and token usage reporting (read-only keys for your side).

Rate limiting and bursting guidance (trial):
- Default soft concurrency quota: 20 concurrent requests per key (suitable for the 20 RPS steady-state you mentioned).
- Default burst allowance: up to 60 RPS for short spikes (configurable for trial).
- Token-based cost accounting under the hood, but rate limits are enforced per-request/RPS and per-minute quotas.
- For your 350 requests/min batch spikes, we'll provision a temporary increased burst bucket during the eval window.

Latency and sizing notes:
- With your average token size (~120) and streaming enabled, p95 < 400ms is achievable in Hosted with autoscaling; if you see consistent 1k+ RPS then Dedicated is recommended.
- Prefix caching and our KV cache will cut repeated prompt costs — we can enable this for your repeat system prompts.

PHI / data controls:
- Hosted: TLS in transit, encryption at rest, isolated keys per customer, 90-day default logs retention. For regulated PHI workloads we recommend either: (a) Hosted with contractually strengthened retention/KMS controls (we can offer an addendum), or (b) Redwood Dedicated / Private for strict on-prem/VPC requirements. We'll flag the SLA questionnaire items that must be escalated to Legal.

Attachments: hosted-rateplan-matrix.pdf (shows our burst/soft/hard limits and pricing impact).

Suggested next steps:
1) Rachel: provision trial keys and share onboarding playbook with Alex.
2) Alex: confirm which endpoints to include in the eval and share any sample prompts that should be tested with streaming.
3) Tech kickoff: 30 min next Tue/Thu — Marcus + Stephanie + Alex + Sarah to provision and run first smoke tests.

If helpful I can also run a quick pressure test with your sample CSV to validate p95 before the kickoff.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
